name: Range Resources Corporation

profile.description: Range Resources Corporation is an independent natural gas, NGL and oil producer focused on the Marcellus Shale in the Appalachian Basin [10]. Q3 2026 production averaged 2.50 Bcfe/d (~68% natural gas) with record NGL output of 133,173 bbl/d, net income of $175.3M ($0.75/share) and operating cash flow of $307.6M [1]. On October 26, 2026, EQT agreed to acquire Range in an all-stock deal (0.987 EQT shares per Range share; Range holders to own ~27% of a combined company with $50B+ enterprise value), expected to close in Q1 2027 [2][3].

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Over the last five years Range has refined rather than reinvented its Marcellus model, the most notable development being record NGL production of 133,173 bbl/d in Q3 2026 [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered operations or quantified AI savings were found in company disclosures or coverage [4]. Market Share (1/2): Range is a major Appalachian gas producer at 2.50 Bcfe/d, but it is being acquired by the larger EQT, so it is a meaningful player rather than the category leader [1][2]. Pipeline (1/2): Management has cited early-phase activity on gas-fired power for Pennsylvania data centers, including a reported partnership with Liberty Energy in Washington County, but no contracted volumes or timelines were disclosed [4]. R&D (0/1): Range reports no R&D spending [11].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Range describes itself as an independent natural gas, NGL and oil company operating in Appalachia — a business description rather than a purpose, interchangeable with basin peers [10]. Community Impact (0/2): Research surfaced no quantified community or charitable program; instead it found a record of Pennsylvania enforcement actions, including a $4.15M impoundment penalty, a $1.75M water-recordkeeping settlement and a 2020 no-contest plea to environmental crimes [6][7][8]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was identified; the company itself repurchased no shares in Q3 2026 [1].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on all 7 growth-sleeve metrics with a perfect weighted sum of 10.0 of 10. D/E of 18.8% (net debt only ~$794M: $500M notes plus $294M on the revolver), ROE of 19.6%, revenue growth of 19.7% YoY, a 5-yr revenue CAGR of 10.9% (FY2020 $1.78B to FY2025 $2.99B, computed), forward P/E of 13.1, profit margin of 26.2% and Yahoo's PEG of 0.97 all meet or beat their targets [1][10][11]. Note that the 5-year base is the 2020 gas-price trough and revenue has swung from $5.33B (2022) to $2.35B (2024), so the metrics are strongly cyclical; liquidity is ample at ~$187M of daily dollar volume [11][10].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Range extracts and sells physical natural gas and NGLs — a commodity AI cannot substitute — and S&P Global and BCG both project that AI data centers will require additional natural gas for power generation, a demand tailwind for Appalachian supply [5][4]. It stops short of 9 because its earnings remain tied to commodity prices rather than contracted AI demand. AI Opportunity (0/1): Data center gas-to-power projects in Pennsylvania remain early-phase with no quantified AI-linked revenue [4].

infinite_game.summary: Range was a Marcellus pioneer, but today it plays a commodity-cycle game: it cut and then suspended its dividend in 2020, rebuilt the balance sheet, and has now agreed to sell itself to EQT, ending its independent existence [2][10]. Sinek would see a disciplined operator optimizing value for shareholders rather than a company organized around a cause that outlives any single deal, and its history of Pennsylvania environmental violations undercuts trust with the communities it operates in [6][8].

just_cause.analysis: Range frames its role around producing natural gas, NGLs and oil in Appalachia, with no articulated vision of a better future state guiding strategy [10]. The agreement to merge into EQT confirms the company's purpose is ultimately shareholder value realization (1/3) [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Range operates with a lean ~564-person workforce and no reported cultural red flags or mass layoffs in the research reviewed [10]. No tenure, turnover or culture evidence distinguishes it as a high-trust organization (1/2).

worthy_rivals.analysis: No management commentary was found framing rivals as benchmarks for improvement; the competitive story ends in consolidation with its largest basin rival, EQT [2][3]. Insufficient evidence of an infinite competitive mindset (0/1).

existential_flexibility.analysis: Range has remained a pure Appalachian gas and NGL producer and, rather than evolving its model toward integrated power or data center supply, has chosen to be acquired [1][2]. Sinek would score this as rigid (0/2).

courage_to_lead.analysis: Leadership showed discipline by suspending the dividend after 2019 to repair the balance sheet, then reinstating it in 2022, and now holds net debt to ~$794M while keeping capital spending at ~25% of budget per quarter [1][10]. That is prudent, but selling to EQT at a ~21% initial premium is the conventional path rather than a costly long-term bet (1/2) [3].

investment_thesis: Range is a low-cost, low-leverage Appalachian gas producer delivering strong results: Q3 2026 net income rose to $175.3M ($0.75/share) from $144.3M, operating cash flow climbed $60M to $307.6M, NGL output hit a record, and net debt is only ~$794M [1]. The pending all-stock sale to EQT (0.987 EQT shares per Range share) gives Range holders ~27% of a $50B+ enterprise-value gas leader positioned to supply Northeast data center power demand that S&P Global expects to require additional natural gas [2][3][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that RRC is now a merger-arbitrage proxy for EQT: the ~21% announcement premium has been roughly halved by EQT's ~8% post-deal drop, and the fixed exchange ratio means RRC's price will track EQT and gas prices until the expected Q1 2027 close [3]. If shareholder approvals or regulatory review fail, Range reverts to a commodity-exposed standalone whose revenue swung from $5.33B (2022) to $2.35B (2024), with a legacy of Pennsylvania environmental enforcement actions [6][11].
key_catalysts: Completion of the EQT all-stock merger (0.987 EQT shares per Range share), expected Q1 2027, pending Range and EQT shareholder votes and an S-4/joint proxy [2][3]
Pennsylvania gas-fired power projects for data centers — including the reported Liberty Energy partnership in Washington County — that could lift Appalachian in-basin demand and pricing [4][5]
Record NGL production (133,173 bbl/d in Q3 2026) and realized pricing of $3.43/mcfe after hedges supporting cash margins of $1.52/mcfe [1]
key_risks: Merger-related: RRC trades with EQT under a fixed exchange ratio, so EQT share weakness or deal failure would directly hit RRC holders [3]
Commodity price volatility — revenue fell from $5.33B in 2022 to $2.35B in 2024 as gas prices collapsed, and could do so again [11]

Environmental and regulatory exposure in Pennsylvania, including past record penalties, a quietly settled $8.9M methane-migration case, and 2020 criminal charges resolved by a no-contest plea [6][7][8]
